title: quantization-nan-triage-scratchpad-maya
content:
Scratchpad / breadcrumbs for NaN / quality regressions when running INT8/FP8/BF16 quantized models

Summary:
- Intermittent NaNs seen during generation when using INT8 quantization path on A100 (cuda 12.x).
- Reproduces ~1/20 runs on long sequences (>1024) for model_xxl-int8 quantized with our offline calibration.
- FP8 conversion experiments also occasionally show INF/NaN in attention logits. BF16 baseline does not produce NaNs.

Observed behaviour (examples):
- Symptoms: final tokens show "nan" in logits printed, generation stalls, pipeline throws RuntimeError: CUDA kernel produced NaN.
- Quick log excerpt: 
  2026-02-26 13:42:11,011 | gen | INFO | step=105 seq_len=1536 topk=40
  2026-02-26 13:42:11,032 | runtime | ERROR | kernel forward_attn: NaN at output_tensor[0][12][34]
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File \"/opt/redwood/runtime/inference.py\", line 842, in _step
      out = self.attn_module(x, kv_cache)
    RuntimeError: CUDA failure: device-side assert triggered - kernel produced NaN

Commands & experiments tried so far:
1) Reproduce minimal local test (deterministic seed)
- python -u tests/repro_nan.py --model model_xxl --seq-len 1536 --seed 42 --quant int8 --num-iter 200
- Result: reproduced on my workstation (A100), run 3/30 seeds produced NaN.

2) Toggle KV-cache flags
- disabled caching: export RW_DISABLE_KV_CACHE=1 && python ...
- Result: NaN frequency dropped (0/30) -> suggests KV cache reuse might interact with quantization paths.

3) Compare quant backends
- INT8 paths: our quant lib (rw-quant), intel-q, and torch.quantization simulated.
- Command: python tools/quant_eval.py --backend rw-quant --model model_xxl --calib calib.npz
- Result: rw-quant shows NaN, others did not for same inputs (but slower).

4) Check calibration distribution & outliers
- inspect calib.npz histograms (scale per-channel) -> found heavy tail in some attention projection channels (max/median ratio > 1e4)
- Hypothesis: calibration outliers cause extremely small scales -> saturating zeros/clipping leading to fp->int overflow on some kernels.

5) Run with Q debug envs (internal hooks)
- export RW_QUANT_DEBUG=1 RW_QUANT_CLAMP_EPS=1e-6
- Observed division by zero warnings in quantize_kernel (scale computed ~0.0 for channel c=17).

6) FP8 experiments
- convert to fp8 (E4M3) using tools/convert_fp8.sh then run same gen script.
- Result: occasional NaN but less frequent; behaviour differs by batch-size and seq-len.

7) Run without compiler optimizations
- torch.compile disabled (set TORCH_COMPILE=0) -> NaNs disappear in 8/10 runs.
- Suggests JIT/fused kernel interaction.

Quick diffs/notes:
- BF16 path (native bf16 kernels) never produced NaNs on same hardware/inputs.
- When forcing forward pass to run on CPU (fallback) no NaNs -> likely GPU kernel-specific.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Calibration outliers + per-channel scale underflow causing divide-by-zero or extremely large inverse scale -> NaN after multiplication (most likely)
2) Fused CUDA kernel bug: quantized attention kernel (fused softmax + scaling) has edge-case with denormals/inf when scale very small (supported by disappearance when torch.compile=0)
3) KV cache pointer reuse bug + quant path mismatch: stale cached keys in different FP format leading to invalid values when reloaded (supported by drop in NaN freq when cache disabled)
4) Race condition / uninitialized memory in custom CUDA kernel under certain batch/seq layouts (hard to rule out)

Immediate mitigations tried (and results):
- clamp scales to minimum epsilon=1e-6 -> reduces NaN rate significantly but some numerical quality degradation (small).
- fallback to BF16 for attention if any channel has scale ratio > 1e3 -> no NaNs in 100 runs, acceptable perf hit.

Detailed commands and snippets used while triaging:
- Inspect calib: python - <<'PY'
import numpy as np
c = np.load('calib.npz')
print({k: (v.max(), v.mean(), (v.max()/ (v.mean()+1e-12))) for k,v in c.items()})
PY

- Run runtime with verbose quant logs: RW_QUANT_DEBUG=1 RW_QUANT_LOG=full python -u serve.py --model model_xxl --quant int8 --port 1234
- Grep for zeros: grep -n "scale=0.0" logs/quant_debug.log | head

- Temporary patch applied to quant kernel (clamp scale):
  scale = max(scale, 1e-6);
  inv_scale = 1.0f / scale;
  // recompile: python build_ext.py --force && pip install -e .

Open questions / things to check next:
- Re-run with trimmed calibration excluding last 0.1% of activations (clipping outliers) and evaluate perplexity/regression on eval set. Measure quality delta.
- Instrument KV cache write/read to verify format (fp16 vs int8 dequantized) at read-time. Add assertion in runtime.
- Reproduce entirely on a different driver/cuda version (cuda 11.8 vs 12.x) to rule out runtime/cuda bug.
- Create minimal fused-kernel repro that triggers NaN (small model with same kernel layout) and file a cutlass/ROCm/driver issue if reproducible.
- Add debug mode to dump pre-softmax logits to disk for failing runs (so we can inspect magnitude distribution).

Planned experiments (short list):
- [ ] Run calibrations with robust quantile clipping (e.g., 99.9th percentile) and compare
- [ ] Add scale epsilon clamp in quant lib + unit tests for zero/missing channels
- [ ] Re-run on non-A100 GPU (V100/RTX) to check HW-specific kernel behaviour
- [ ] Bisect to find earliest commit that introduced NaNs (binary search on serving-runtime commits)
- [ ] Add runtime fallback path: on NaN detection, retry step with BF16 for that layer and log stack.

Notes-to-self (todo details):
- If fallback reduces throughput too much, consider per-model policy: allow BF16 fallback only for long sequences or models with >X channels with bad calibration.
- Talk to infra to get access to one of the older nodes with cuda11 for cross-check.
- Add unit test that simulates scale=0 channel to ensure quant lib clamps and does not divide by zero.

Relevant links/refs:
- ENG-9876 (internal ticket tracking this regression)
- PR with temporary clamp: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/732
- Confluence investigation notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Quantization+NaN+investigation

Bottom line / current status:
- Root cause not confirmed. Strong suspicion on calibration outliers combined with fused CUDA kernel edge-case.
- Low-risk mitigation (clamping scales + quantile clipping during calibration) has been implemented as temp fix in PR 732; needs perf/quality validation across models.
- Next: run wide validation (10 models) with clamp and quantile clipping, then roll to dedicated staging cluster if pass.

Breadcrumbs / quick references for whoever picks up:
- Repro script: tests/repro_nan.py
- Calib files: /data/quant/calib/model_xxl_calib.npz
- Patch candidate branch: fix/quant-clamp-2026-02

-- maya
